title: Similarity search not working well when number of ingested documents is great, say over one hundred.
body:
When few documets embedded into vector db everything works fine, with similarity search I can always find the most relevant documents on the top of results. But when it comes to over hundred, searching result will be very confusing, given the same query I could not find any relevant documents. I've tried Chroma, Faiss, same story.

Anyone has any idea? thanks.
btw, the documents are in Chinese...

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Yeah, I experience the same. I think it's related to the embedding method used. In my experience, OpenAI embedding seems to work better than the ones from HuggingFace.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
i'm having similar issues with English content using `LlamaCppEmbeddings`. in fact, most relevant document is often the last or second to last document in the list which makes it essentially impossible to do question answering with document context using `LlamaCpp`.

i've tried `Chroma`, `FAISS` and `DataLake` vectorstores. i've also tried `similarity_search` and `max_marginal_relevance` with vector based and text based inputs. all seem to suffer from this problem which leads me to believe that it's an issue with `LlamaCppEmbeddings`

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
testing with the default embedding function `SentenceTransformerEmbeddingFunction` and i'm getting far more predictable and reasonable output from `similarity_search` with `Chroma`.

it's surprising to me that `LlamaCppEmbeddings` is doing such a poor job. i'll be filing a ticket with llama-cpp-python because i don't see how the problem could be with the very simple implementation in langchain -- it is doing almost nothing itself.

I posted a question to another thread but think this might be useful here too. The sentence transformers have a truncation length and I suspect that if the text splitter creates document that are larger that what the embedding model can ingest, the embeddings will be of poor quality.

Sadly, the multilingual sentence transformers all have a truncation length of 128 tokens !

See my question here: https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/issues/2026#issuecomment-1601097513

comments.author: participant10
comments.body:
Met the same issue
The way our team handled it is to first reduce search space/document number by labeling the docs(by the "abstract" or something) in advance and do vector similarity search for those labels, and then do the similarity search in the reduced space. 
Also the way you split documentation is very important, the longer the chunks the more difficult to match that key word. So we have tried to split the chunks by fixed number of characters to make the chunks smaller.

Hope this helps!

comments.author: participant13
comments.body: Vector representation works great with frequent entries but gives poor results at the tail of query distribution. In such cases, a simple keyword yields better IR.

comments.author: participant14
comments.body: Workaround I found is to purge vector db from memory and create a new vectorstore each time for a new doc in a loop. Not time efficient but guarantees high precision.

comments.author: participant15
comments.body: While I'm glad you are satisfied with your code, I must note that if you are resetting your index for each vectorstore on the fly then you have no need for a vectorstore in the first place. It also does nothing to address the OP's issue of low retriever recall on larger corpora, which is improved through a mixture of better feature representation and better querying.

comments.author: participant14
comments.body: @participant15 agreed, that's a valid point. However splitting documents and doing similarity search is easy and precise with Langchain chroma vectorstore. I couldn't find better alternatives without creating a vector store.

comments.body: Ok, I am having a same scenario. Using Azure OpenAI with Ada embedding and storing in Milvus db. There is only 13 pages in the PDF. There is a relative text in page 8, whatever or however I ask a relevant in question in that page, it is not returning the content. comments.author: participant14
comments.body:
@participant16 even I have over 1000 PDFs with each over 20 pages and I use [these](https://<redacted-host>/gpt4all_python_embedding.html) Open Source embedding models. 
For 1 or few retrievals per PDF, @participant15 's elegant and short vector similarity solution works for me. One can play with that in a loop for multiple PDFs, focus on 1 PDF at a time, rather than storing everything in a vector store, as he suggested.
For multiple PDFs and multiple queries in each PDF, above solution + using a NoSQL type store to cache the retrieved content for each query in a PDF makes sense. You will have everything in one pace but isolated, for repeated querying. You can set the keys as PDF names/ID and values as a dictionary of queries and corresponding retrieved content in each PDFs. This is a scalable as well. Basically extract and store content out of each PDF for all queries, in an isolated manner.

Second approach, use vector store, as you did. But when you move to different PDF, it is wise to purge the embeddings out of memory, else you will be doing similarity search in older cached embeddings. Otherwise, follow [this ](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/17410)

Secondly, after you extract texts out of PDFs, I suggest you to experiment with size of split / partitions of the texts. Making the split size similar to size of text to be retrieved, can help. Experiment with increased overlapping as well (incase of big size of text to be retrieved). Forming the query with closest match to that text can help too (if this has to be generalized, such as in a chatbot, you might want to come up with a smarter way of writing queries).
